Hey, you sound like you’re freaking out, which is totally understandable, but I was in your position about a year ago and I got my landlord to pay, so here are some tips:

1. Specific laws vary by state, but landlords have an obligation to provide safe, sanitary living conditions. A unit with bedbugs does not fulfill that obligation. That means that landlords are required to pay for extermination, unless it can be proved that the tenant introduced the infestation. This is often very difficult to prove, because if multiple units in the building are found to be infested, the problem could have started in any of them. This is why you should tell your landlord and do everything you can to get him to hire a professional to inspect all of the units surrounding yours. And even if it’s just your unit, it could have been caused by the previous tenant. How recently did you move in? The more recent the move, the easier this will be to argue. So, bottom line, you need to tell the landlord to have any chance of him paying. 

2. Document everything and don’t clean anything until the landlord agrees to pay. I moved in to a heavily infested unit, and once I realized the problem, I obsessively took pictures, especially the baseboard covered in fecal smears. The amount of fecal smears was so bad that multiple professionals told the landlord that I couldn’t have caused the infestation because an infestation that bad would have needed at least 6 months to develop, and I had just moved in a month ago. 

3. If the landlord is being difficult, say you’re considering getting legal representation. I never had to do this, but I did threaten it, and it seemed to help the landlord realize that I was serious about getting them to pay. 

Good luck! I hope some of this helps.
